Jessica Marshall's mystery Tower of Doom partner and the UWF's own newest signing, billing himself as the man who beat Chris Blue and ended Chris Courtade's career; escaped the cage on 30 October 2004 as part of the winning team alongside Edmond Winston IV, Victor Frost, and Papa Legba in his own first UWF match, though Winston used him as muscle against Alex Extreme and Alex Martinez along the way. Beat "Dark Horse" Randall Osbourne by pinfall (the Lowlife Driver, an inverted DDT) on 3 November 2004 in his own first singles match for the wing, mocking the former heavyweight champion as washed up beforehand. Beat Steve Ryott by pinfall (the Cherry Pop Drop, a double underhook facebuster) on 27 November 2004, mocking the newcomer beforehand as a nobody and surviving a springboard dropkick exchange along the way. Beat Jason Keening by pinfall (a reverse cradle with his feet illegally on the ropes) on 11 December 2004 after proposing a weapons-free technical contest himself; learned backstage that Becky Byers had booked him against "The Last American Badass" Alex Martinez at Rise to Power, with a UWF World Heavyweight Championship shot attached if Martinez beat Kyle Lee that same night. Accepted Edmond Winston IV's own gift of the New Era on 28 May 2005, immediately putting Jamie Underwood through a bomb-squad beatdown with his own new recruits Corporate Leverage and Joey~!, then turned Strictly Business against Underwood as well and renamed the faction the Illuminati. Fought Alex Kidd to a double countout on 11 June 2005 after both men refused to break outside the ring, then called off the surrounding Illuminati and let Kidd leave unharmed, calling the veteran's own showing worthy of respect. Mocked Alex Kidd and Alex Extreme in an Illuminati promo backstage on 23 July 2005 alongside Andrew Tucker, then lost to Extreme by count-out after walking out of their match at Joey~!'s prompting. Led the Illuminati in mocking the Pride, the Youngbloods, and a returning Alex Kidd at Brawl From The Mall 6 on 6 August 2005, then was beaten down alongside Strictly Business by Kidd and the Fraternity Boys. Teamed with Tigress in the Cupid's Revenge Blind Date Tournament on 14 February 2006, interfering with a chair on both remaining finalists after his own team's elimination and inadvertently helping Alex Extreme pin Jason Keening. Demanded a World Heavyweight Championship shot on 18 March 2006, citing his own pinfall win over Alex Martinez at Rise to Power, and was named to a four-way title match the following week against Martinez, Brett Greene, and Alex Extreme after Becky Byers denied him the sole shot.

Billed from Los Angeles, California, with his brother Michael Keening as the Ghost Dancers, the reigning UWF World Tag Team Champions; retained by default when their three-way title defense was ruled a no-contest on 9 August 2003. Lost the UWF World Tag Team Championship to Team Canada on 4 October 2003 after Kari Stevens pepper-sprayed him at ringside; the Privateers ambushed both brothers backstage afterward. Won the UWF North American Tag Team Championship with his brother from Team Canada by submission on 25 October 2003, after a contract clause kept the World Tag Team Championship off the line. Lost the UWF North American Tag Team Championship on 15 November 2003 when teammates Erik and Chad Grimsson escaped the Tower of Doom cage as a complete team before he and his brother Michael could. Entered the 20 December 2003 twelve-man elimination match with brother Michael; tagged in late by Alex Extreme to help finish off Jacob Drake with a Hart Attack combination, winning the match and the right to help set his own side's Eve of Destruction stipulations alongside Extreme. Teamed with brother Michael and Erik Grimsson on 10 March 2004 in a six-man tag loss to Team Canada and Scott Daniels after two unidentified men in suits ambushed the match. Challenged Victor Frost for the UWF North American Heavyweight Championship on 24 March 2004, losing by pinfall (Death Valley Driver) after Frost blinded him with fingerpaint smuggled in by manager Simone Sumner. Teamed with brother Michael again as the Ghost Dancers on 29 May 2004, fighting Serge Annis and Caliban to a double countout after trading big moves at ringside; the Privateers ran in on the ensuing brawl, and commissioner Becky Byers added the Ghost Dancers to the Gold Rush UWF World Tag Team Championship match against champions the Privateers and Annis and Caliban. Teamed with brother Michael as the Ghost Dancers in a losing Gold Rush triple threat for the UWF World Tag Team Championship on 5 June 2004, his own brother pinned by Jacob Drake of the champion Privateers; assaulted backstage afterward by a mystery masked attacker while Michael was taken to a hospital for a back injury suffered in the match. Beat Scott "Hotspot" Daniels by pinfall (an inside cradle) on 28 August 2004 in his own first UWF singles match; attacked after the bell by Daniels and then by a masked man who revealed himself as "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas -- the same man who had attacked his brother Michael backstage at Gold Rush -- before Daniels drove Douglas from the ring. Lost a three-way dance to Scott "Hotspot" Daniels on 16 October 2004, pinned by a stolen cover after colliding head-first with Chris Douglas. Beat Chris Douglas's own bodyguard Titanicus by pinfall (a bridging Northern Lights suplex) on 27 November 2004 despite Douglas's own repeated ringside coaching and interference, only to be blindsided afterward by a Douglas Dragon suplex once the bout was won. Lost to Luke Kinsey by pinfall (a reverse cradle, feet on the ropes) on 11 December 2004 in a match Kinsey had proposed as a clean technical contest, then was whip-strapped by Chris Douglas and Titanicus afterward, setting up a strap match at Rise to Power; briefly reconciled with Rick Marley backstage. Lost to UWF newcomer Ethan de Sade by pinfall (the Ghostbuster) on 28 May 2005 after a pre-match beatdown from de Sade's father, Chris Douglas, and Douglas's own bodyguard, Titanicus; demanded a handicap rematch against both Douglas and de Sade from Jessica "Fatality" Marshall afterward, still bloodied. Traded insults with Alex Extreme outside a sports bar on 11 June 2005, then teamed with him in a tag loss to Chris Douglas and Ethan de Sade after Extreme accidentally clotheslined him, and brawled with Extreme afterward until Chris Douglas and de Sade jumped both men. Smashed a locker room mirror over his own rivalry with Alex Extreme on 22 June 2005, reassured by visiting uncle "Fireball" Ken Keening that Extreme's own past attack on him was not Jason's own fight to settle. Shared a Memphis jail cell with Alex Extreme on 6 July 2005 after their own brawl during the Road to the Gold, and learned from Ken Keening that Extreme's earlier attack on him had been staged to provoke Jason. Answered children's questions about his own feud with Alex Extreme at a community center appearance on 20 July 2005, calling Extreme "scum" and naming Chris Douglas and Ethan de Sade as also deserving a reckoning. Warned by Sabbath backstage on 23 July 2005 about the dangers of his own hatred for Extreme; lost a random-partners tag match teamed with Miguel Quesada against Michael Augustine and Victor Frost the same show, pinned by a cradle brainbuster. Eliminated second from the main event eight-man elimination match on 3 August 2005, chokeslammed by Tumaffi after sniping on-camera with teammate Alex Extreme. Teamed with Lisa Drake in the Cupid's Revenge Blind Date Tournament on 14 February 2006, eliminating Luke Kinsey and Tigress before being pinned by Alex Extreme after Kinsey's own post-elimination chair shots left both finalists dazed.

Billed from Dortmund, Germany, weighing 268 pounds; climbed the guardrail mid-match to threaten the crowd with a chair after being speared out of the ring, then pinned Pierce Bleed with a top-rope superbomb in a non-title singles match. Beat Tragedy by pinfall (electric chair drop) on 12 November 2003, earning a future UWF North American Heavyweight Championship shot. Won the 17 December 2003 fifteen-man battle royal to open the Meltdown Championship tournament, throwing Paul Wong with a Samoan drop for the final elimination, then lost the semi-finals to Papa Legba, pinned by an inverted DDT after injuring his own arm on a missed elbowdrop. Retained the UWF North American Heavyweight Championship over "Screaming Drillbit" Jason Keening on 24 March 2004 by pinfall (Death Valley Driver) after blinding him with fingerpaint smuggled in by manager Simone Sumner. Billed as the reigning UWF North American Heavyweight Champion on 29 May 2004, though no surviving document in the held record states when or how he won the title from its prior holder, Kyle Lee; abandoned his own title defense against a substituting Chris O'Brien to chase down a returning Quinn Brown, losing by countout, though the title did not change hands. Brawled with Brown into the parking garage afterward and was thrown through the windshield of his own car. Retained the UWF North American Heavyweight Championship over Quinn Brown by pinfall (the Violator Mark II) at Gold Rush on 5 June 2004, after Brown's own manager Victoria Marquess shoved Brown off the top rope and then revealed a secret alliance with Frost, kissing him after the match. Beat November by pinfall (a steel chair shot) in a non-title match on 18 September 2004 after manager Victoria Marquess revealed the bout had been arranged with no disqualifications; valets Roxy Mayhem and Simone Sumner interfered throughout. Escaped a Tower of Doom cage match on 30 October 2004 as part of the winning team alongside Edmond Winston IV, Papa Legba, and Luke Kinsey, though the match ended in chaos after the bell when a returning "Doomsayer" Kyle Lee attacked Winston. Retained the UWF North American Heavyweight Championship over Quinn Brown by pinfall (a high-elevation Death Valley Driver) on 13 November 2004, after Roxy Mayhem pulled fellow Violence Girl Simone Sumner into Brown's path to save himself from a missile dropkick. Retained the UWF North American Heavyweight Championship over Uriah Hawkins by pinfall on 17 November 2004, hanging onto the top rope as Hawkins's own Suicide DDT attempt drove Hawkins's head into the mat instead. Fired manager Victoria Marquess on 27 November 2004 after she confronted him over abandoning her and Simone Sumner; Marquess revealed before leaving that she had already signed a mystery challenger for Frost's own UWF North American Heavyweight Championship at Rise to Power. Pressed Jessica Marshall backstage on 11 December 2004 to reveal the mystery challenger signed by his own former manager Victoria Marquess for his UWF North American Heavyweight Championship defense at Rise to Power, learning only that the contract was airtight; separately, Papa Legba signed to challenge him for the same title. Debuted a new manager, Roxy Mayhem, and the "Graphic Violence World Tour 2005" on 28 May 2005, refusing an open challenge from "The Walking Contradiction" Sabbath as beneath his own standards. Traded barbs with Sayaka Daikin-Price backstage on 11 June 2005 with manager Roxy Mayhem at his side, then beat a returning Alex Martinez by pinfall (a chair-assisted spike piledriver, feet on the ropes) after Roxy Mayhem rang the ring bell early to trick Martinez into thinking he had already won. Dismissed Alex Martinez's own Road to the Gold win to reporter Peter Phillips on 6 July 2005 as an injustice, vowing to "liberate" the Unified Television Championship from Marcus Nuit; lost the title match by disqualification after Sabbath ran in and attacked him. Revealed in a hospital-room scene on 20 July 2005 to have been scalped bald by Sabbath's own recent attack, along with valet Roxy Mayhem, whom he blamed for the humiliation; vowed revenge on Sabbath. Teamed with Michael Augustine to beat Miguel Quesada and Jason Keening on 23 July 2005. Survived the main event eight-man elimination match on 3 August 2005 alongside Tumaffi, pinning Sabbath last with a Death Valley Driver after tripping his own partner's top-rope attempt. Returned on 18 March 2006 after a four-month absence, publicly dumped valet Roxy Mayhem, and declared himself number-one contender to the World Heavyweight Championship by replaying his own July 2005 pinfall over Alex Martinez; denied a title shot and booked for a match the following week by an angry Becky Byers. Lost to Corey Irons by pinfall (the Lariat) on 7 June 2006, unable to hold a dragon sleeper as Irons powered to his feet.
